purpose: a strict necessary condition gives Yes / No / Unknown / contested for immediate executability, with the proof obligations named
text: There is a robot hand. Block a is on the table. Block a is clear. The hand is empty. The hand can take a block only if the block is red.

units.text: Block a is on the table.
The hand can take a block only if the block is red.

must_have.note: every clause with a positive poss(take(...)) head conjoins the ok_take hook, and ok_take requires restriction_S5; this replaces a blanket ban on positive poss heads, which would also match the correct rule

must_not_have.note: the restriction must not be rewritten to can (A4.2)

queries.text: Can the hand take block a now?

expect.evidence: base text: red(a) is unsupported. The positive path needs the check restriction_1_S5, which needs +red(a) at W0; the negative path needs -red(a) at W0. Neither exists. Absence is not No (A2.3).

variants.text: There is a robot hand. Block a is on the table. Block a is clear. Block a is red. The hand is empty. The hand can take a block only if the block is red.

expect.evidence: the library default poss_take_hand: isa block a, empty(hand), clear_top(a) and on(a,table) at W0, and ok_take through restriction_1_S5 with +red(a) at W0

variants.text: There is a robot hand. Block a is on the table. Block a is clear. Block a is not red. The hand is empty. The hand can take a block only if the block is red.

expect.evidence: the necessity_restriction clause of S5 with -red(a) at W0. No positive poss path exists (the hook fails). The No comes from an accepted negative proof, not from the missing positive proof.

variants.text: There is a robot hand. Block a is on the table. Block a is clear. Block a is red. Block a is not red. The hand is empty. The hand can take a block only if the block is red.

expect.evidence: both +poss (via +red) and -poss (via -red) have accepted support; A2.3: contested permission is not a validated action; the answer is neither Yes nor No. GK's contradiction tolerance may report either proof; the route must report both.

candidates.reason: restriction satisfied (red true); mechanical preconditions true
restriction S5 unsupported; replay needs positive support for every applicable restriction (A5.1); the candidate is not validated. This is 'not validated', not 'proved impossible'.

explain: The Stage-2 form follows A3.2's own example for this sentence: executable(take(hand 1,X)) -> red(X), with no isa(block,X) in the antecedent. The class scope is supplied by take's own applicability law, which already requires isa(block,X) on every positive path; a translation that adds isa(block,X) to the antecedent is also accepted, and then the guard is preserved in the compiled clauses (REVIEW.md disposition 9; the class-scoped form is tested in c05). The four variants differ in one sentence and pin the four rows of A4.2's table. The structural expectation is path coverage: every positive applicability path of take conjoins the hook, and the necessity clause keeps exactly its condition.
notes: Four variants, one query each. The contested variant is the one where GK's report may differ between builds; the fixture pins that the route reports contested, not whichever proof GK lists first. Amended 2026-09-23 (encoding v2, gold review 0.4): Q2, the underlying-ability contrast, is removed from the base and from all four variants; v2 has one planning predicate and Q1 already tests executability.
